text:
Situation: Corvale General holds 210 units of divalproex sodium with 26 days on hand at current use. The product label names Coupler LLC as the registered plant for this NDC.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 1049813 at Coupler LLC ended on 2018-04-27 and was classified OAI, with the classification known on 2018-07-26. FDA inspection 1120463 at the same plant ended on 2020-03-10 and was also classified OAI, known on 2020-06-08. A Warning Letter was issued to Coupler LLC on 2020-09-15 following those inspections. FDA inspection 1148607 ended on 2021-08-12 and was classified OAI, known on 2021-11-10. The most recent inspection 1308780 ended on 2026-03-02 and was classified VAI, known on 2026-05-27. As of 2026-10-21, divalproex sodium is not listed on the FDA drug shortage list.

Our position: Current inventory provides approximately 26 days of supply. The manufacturing plant has a history of OAI classifications and a Warning Letter, with the most recent inspection showing VAI. The drug is not on the FDA shortage list, but supply continuity risk remains given the inspection history.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to evaluate and place orders with A-S Medication Solutions, ATLANTIC BIOLOGICALS CORP., AbbVie Inc., American Health Packaging, and Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC to diversify supply sources. Approval: Pharmacy Director.
2. Buyer to request plant registration details from each alternate supplier to assess manufacturing site risk. Approval: Pharmacy Director.
3. Buyer to monitor FDA inspection outcomes for Coupler LLC and all alternate supplier plants. Approval: Pharmacy Director.
4. Report supply status and procurement plan to P&T Committee at next scheduled meeting. Approval: P&T Committee Chair.

Not recommended: No clinical protocol changes or therapeutic substitutions at this time.
